summary: John Dowson, who studied under Edwin Norris, worked in indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Royal Asiatic Society (~1845), East India Company College (~1855-1858), Staff College, Camberley (1855-1877), and University College London (1855-1877).

John Drake was an indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Regent's Park College and the University of Oxford (M.A.). He served at Serampore College (1910-1926) and the Saharanpur Theological Seminary (until 1933).
Working in indology and linguistics, John Drew Bate studied at Regent's Park College (~1858-1865). He subsequently served as a member of the Baptist Missionary Society from 1865 to 1897.

John E. Cort is an indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970-1974) and Harvard University (~1980-1984). He became a professor at Denison University (~1993).

John F. Richards worked in indology and history and archaeology, studying at the University of New Hampshire (~1957-1961) and UC Berkeley (~1961-1970). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968-1977) and Duke University (~1977-2007).

Indologist and historian John Faithfull Fleet studied at UCL and under Theodor Goldstücker. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1865-1897), Government of India (1883-1886), and Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland, including as Honorary Secretary (1906-1917).
John Firminger Duthie served as Superintendent of the Saharanpur Botanical Garden (~1876-1902) and Director of the Botanical Survey of India (~1891-1902).

Working in indology, John Forbes Royle studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Saharanpur Botanical Garden (1823-1831), King's College London (1837-1856), and the India Office (~1858).

John Forbes White Youngson was a scholar of linguistics and indology who earned an M.A. and D.D. from the University of Aberdeen. He served as a missionary with the Church of Scotland from 1875 to 1907.

John Frederick Browne studied in the fields of indology and linguistics at Exeter College, Oxford (~1853-1854) and the East India Company College (~1854-1855). In 1858, he held a post in the Bengal Civil Service.

John Frederick Dickson was a scholar in Buddhist studies and indology. He was educated at Westminster School (~1847-1855) and Christ Church, Oxford, where he studied from 1855 to 1859 and received his B.A.

John Garrett worked in indology and linguistics. He served as the first Director of the Central College of Bangalore in 1858 and as Director of Public Instruction for Mysore's Department of Public Instruction in 1871.

Indology and religious studies scholar John George Woodroffe studied at University College, Oxford, and under Sivachandra Vidyarnava. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (1897), Calcutta High Court (~1904-1922), and University of Oxford (1923-1930).

Hangin was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana University Bloomington, where he served as full professor (1965-1989). He also held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, and Columbia.
John Graham Drummond, an indology and linguistics scholar, earned his B.A. (~1903-1906) and Ph.D. (by 1939) at Christ's College, Cambridge. He served there as Lecturer in Bengali in 1936.

John Greenfield Leonard, working in history, archaeology, and indology, earned degrees from Stanford (~1955-1959) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1959-1962). He held posts at Wisconsin-Madison (1967) and the University of California, San Diego (1968-1973).

John Griffiths studied at the Royal College of Art and worked in indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (~1860-1865), Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (1865), and the National College of Arts.
John H. Berthrong, who studied under graduate supervisor Alfonso Verdu, works in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He is attested at Boston University in 1996.
John Hay worked in sinology and studied at the University of Aberdeen, earning an M.A. by 1833. He later served as a Fellow at the University of Madras from 1888 to 1889.

John Henry Hutton studied at Worcester College and the University of Oxford (D.Sc. 1921). Working in indology and history, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909-1937) and as William Wyse Professor at Cambridge (1936-1950).
